So basically I advise against installing any Ubisoft game both on Steam Deck and Steam Machine because you risk losing all of your save games. Long story short - AC Odyssey, AC Origins - both games require you to have the Ubisoft client and an active internet connection in order to start the game (!!), even despite the fact that both are single-player and there is no cross-save functionality (and any sort of online activity is long gone from Origins). There is just no option to disable it; if you choose offline mode in the settings - that will just not work. So each time you launch the game you will see a prompt “syncing your games”. So I have progress (around 30h) on both games, obviously I wanted to see them in whole 120fps 4K HDR glory on a tv screen.  I’ve launched it, logged in to the Ubisoft account, looked into “syncing your saves” messaging from the Ubi client - then in a moment I came to the actual game - there were no save games, only a brand new game option. Then I launched the Steam Deck version - the same. Looks like it’s just erasing your saves the moment you log into the Ubi account from a different device. At the moment Ubi support tells me ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ advices to reinstall my Windows drivers on a steam os, but I want to get from them an official acknowledgement of a problem in order to get a refund from Steam. claims.claim: Reviewers describe the open world of Ancient Egypt as visually stunning, detailed, and atmospheric.

citations.review_text:
🏺 Assassin’s Creed Origins — ancient Egypt, beautiful landscapes and the beginning of something new ⚔️☀️

Assassin’s Creed Origins feels like Ubisoft decided to completely reinvent Assassin’s Creed — and honestly, it mostly worked.

Ancient Egypt is absolutely beautiful. From massive cities and forgotten tombs to endless deserts and the Nile, the world feels alive and incredibly atmospheric. Exploring it was easily one of my favorite parts of the game.

I went into Origins expecting a classic Assassin’s Creed experience, but what I got was something much closer to an open-world RPG.

🔥 Gameplay & Atmosphere

✅ The world — absolutely stunning. Egypt is huge, detailed and full of places worth exploring. Riding through the desert, climbing ancient monuments and discovering hidden tombs never gets old.

✅ Combat — a massive improvement over the older games. The new hitbox-based system makes fights much more active and satisfying instead of simply countering enemies over and over again.

✅ Bayek — easily one of the best protagonists in the franchise. He's charismatic, emotional and actually feels like a real person rather than just another assassin.

✅ Ancient Egypt — probably the biggest reason to play this game. The setting is incredible, and the attention to historical details makes exploration genuinely fascinating.

✅ The soundtrack and atmosphere — fantastic. There are moments when you can simply ride through the desert, listen to the music and forget you're even playing a game.

🏺 The Story

The story has some genuinely great moments.

Bayek's personal journey gives the game an emotional core, and his relationship with Aya is one of the strongest parts of the narrative.

The problem is that the main story can sometimes feel inconsistent. Some parts are incredibly emotional and memorable, while others feel like they're just there to fill the enormous open world.

And that's where Origins starts showing its weaknesses.

Assassin's Creed Origins is a difficult one to review.

The combat is, in my opinion, the worst I've experienced in an Assassin's Creed game. It feels clunky, and it took away from a lot of the enjoyment I could have had during encounters. The progression system also doesn't help, as the constant need to farm materials and resources becomes more of a chore than something enjoyable.

The microtransactions are another downside. They constantly take away from the experience and make the game feel less rewarding. Instead of simply enjoying the adventure, there is always that feeling that the game is pushing you toward shortcuts or extra purchases.

That being said, the rest of the game does a lot to make up for it. The world is easily one of the best Ubisoft has created. If you're interested in Ancient Egypt, this game is a simple purchase. The attention to detail, the landscapes, and the atmosphere are incredible. Exploring the pyramids, deserts, and ancient cities is where this game truly shines.

The story is often praised as one of the best in the series, but personally, I don't fully see it. It's a pretty standard revenge story, and while it's enjoyable enough, there wasn't much that felt completely new or surprising to me.

One thing I will always appreciate, though, is the wildlife. The hippos especially are a highlight and somehow manage to be both terrifying and entertaining at the same time.

Overall, Assassin's Creed Origins is a mixed experience. The world and setting are fantastic, but the combat, resource farming, and microtransactions hold it back. I wouldn't pay full price for it, but if you can pick it up for around $10, especially if you enjoy Ancient Egypt and exploration, it's worth a look.

citations.review_text:
Although I personally prefer Valhalla followed by Odyssey, Origins was the first of the RGB formula that in my opinion saved the franchise from stagnation. 
Also, Bayek, Aya and Layla are awesome and the fourth main character of this game is Egypt itself which is beautifully recreated. Discovery Tour is also very well done and I'm glad they made them up until Valhalla
DLCs add depth and new locations as well. 
The biggest complaint I have is that cutscenes tend to be "stuttery" throughout the entire game even though gameplay and frametime are perfectly smooth.

First of all, the game seemed a bit expensive, but when it’s on sale, it’s definitely worth buying. I downloaded it only recently and I quickly became obsessed with it – it’s really fun to play. I’ve had it for just a few weeks and I already have almost 70 hours of playtime.
I’m planning to buy the DLCs as well, but for me they’re a bit too expensive right now, so I’m waiting for a sale. The game also has some negatives, like occasional bugs – sometimes objects get stuck in walls or I can’t walk through something that looks completely normal. For me, the biggest issue is that the game has crashed twice during the hippodrome races, which is pretty annoying because I have to replay the whole thing again.
Overall, Assassin’s Creed Origins is a great game and I definitely recommend it. None of the negatives are bigger than the positives. I like it so much that I already bought another Assassin’s Creed game – hopefully it will be just as good.

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the open-world environment design, citing the detailed depiction of ancient Egypt, its historical architecture, and the transition between deserts and the Nile.

citations.review_text:
My first proper AC game, several uninstalls and finally this time it kicked. My mistake was looking at the damn compass like how I did in Skyrim and visiting every POIs and got burnt out fast. What clicked for me was simply going through the side quests because some of them were really well made and stood out like the mainline story. 

Personally im not a fan of how the combat feels/flows, it sure was fun, the executions were neat and meaty and loved how you get different weapons with its own movesets, but I just couldn't vibe with the animations. 

The world design was probably the 
strongest aspect. Felt very lived in. Loved how they dabbled in the history, lore, the grand architectures, character designs of that era and the minute details that accentuate the Ptolemic Egyptian timeline.

I would end by saying that having played a lot of RPGs, the rpg aspect here was the most uninteresting part for me, I skimmed past most of the mundane stuff and did the bare minimum grind to get past the levelgating.

"59 Hours In and Still Breathless: The Ultimate Historical Playground"

Spending 59 hours in a single-player game usually means you’ve grown tired of its mechanics. With Assassin’s Creed Origins, it’s the exact opposite. After nearly 60 hours exploring Ancient Egypt, I can confidently say this is not just a great Assassin's Creed game—it is a landmark achievement in open-world design.Here is why every single hour was worth it.

The World: A Masterclass in Atmosphere

Living History: Ubisoft didn't just build a map; they built a time machine. The transition from the scorching, shimmering desert dunes to the lush, green banks of the Nile is visually stunning.

Unmatched Scale: Walking through the bustling streets of Alexandria or standing at the foot of the Pyramids feels genuinely awe-inspiring. The level of historical detail packed into every corner is staggering.

[h2][b]In Amun's Name, Egypt Has Never Looked Better And May He Bear Witness, Origins is a Masterpiece.[/b][/h2]

[i][b]"I am not a father anymore.  I am not a husband. I am not a Medjay. I am a Hidden One. [/b][/i]


I can't believe it's been 9 years since this came out, This is my 2nd time playing this game (my 1st playthrough was during Covid and this game kept me sane and it was like my comfort blanket game) and after 100% completing it this time along with all the DLCs and achievements, I can confidently say no game based on Egypt is going to top this game. What Ubisoft has achieved with this world is marvelous. I can get lost in ancient Egypt just roaming around with my horse. For some, this is the best Assassin's Creed and I can get why. It's one of the finest open-world games Ubisoft has ever made. 

The [b]soundtrack[/b] to this game is outstanding. Seriously, just listen to the soundtrack on Spotify or Apple Music. This might be the best AC soundtrack since Black Flag.  

While many fans were divided by the shift from the traditional Assassin's Creed formula to an RPG-inspired experience, I believe that change was exactly what the series needed. After games like Unity and Syndicate, the franchise had started to feel repetitive. Origins breathed new life into it.

[b]Ancient Egypt[/b] is the true star of the game. From the bustling streets of [b]Alexandria[/b] to the endless [b]Sahara[/b], towering [b]pyramids[/b], and lush [b]oases[/b], every corner of the map feels handcrafted and alive. Even years later, it's still one of the most beautiful open worlds I've explored.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the main character Bayek as a well-written, compassionate, and likeable protagonist with genuine motives driving the revenge story.

citations.review_text: After 100 plus hours in game, i still have not done either expansion. Gigantic compared to other RPG franchises, and Bayek (the main character that you play as) becomes very likeable over the 100 plus quests ive done. His motives are genuine (making for a really sad but well told story) and they make you identify with him. Great game 5/5

Assassin's Creed Origins was a really enjoyable experience, especially because I have actually been to Egypt. Seeing places I visited recreated during Ancient Egypt at the height of its civilization was amazing. Walking through Alexandria, Memphis, the pyramids, and the deserts gave me a whole new appreciation for the setting. Ubisoft really did an incredible job bringing Egypt to life.

The main story is good and I really enjoyed Bayek's revenge journey. Bayek is easily one of my favorite Assassin's Creed protagonists, and I also liked Aya whenever she became playable. Their relationship carries the story and gives it a lot of emotional weight. My biggest issue is that the main story feels too short. It feels like only about 30 percent of the game is actually focused on the main plot, while the other 70 percent is side content. I wish there had been more story missions because the revenge plot was one of the strongest parts of the game.

The Hidden Ones DLC was easily my favorite part after the base game. It was great seeing the Brotherhood after the Creed had officially been established. Recruiting new members, expanding the Hidden Ones, and tying up one of the loose ends from the main story made the DLC feel like a proper continuation. It was also nice to see Aya return.

Curse of the Pharaohs was a different experience. The story itself did not really grab me, and once again it felt like most of the content was side quests instead of main missions. However, the mythology and the different afterlife locations were absolutely stunning. Exploring those worlds showed just how creative Ubisoft could be when they were not limited by historical realism.

Combat is where the game disappointed me the most. It is simply too easy. I ended up using a bow build for almost the entire game because headshots would one shot most enemies. I was half-way through Odyssey when I decided to jump on Origins due to story reasons, and what a difference in writing and atmosphere.

While Odyssey let you explore amazing fields of flowers and roam the seas to reach greek islands, Origins offers you pyramids and tombs, deserts and oasises.
Both main stories are good, but Bayek, as a protector, interacts with children and the egyptian people in a  more compassionate way than Kassandra the mercenary. Side stories in Origins are particularly good, unlike Odyssey's feminist pandering and bland fetch quests. 
While Origins mixes combat and infiltration/sneaking pretty well, Odyssey focuses more on combet with a large array of melee and range skills. Origins has limited healing while in combat (aside from the passives on your weapons) while Odyssey has a skill that you can use as much as you like, due to most enemies having way too much health.
Origins' "dungeons" are all varied, while Odyssey has copy-pasted camps and tombs but lets you fight legendary creatures and hunt sect members across the map.

Regarding the missions, objectives and locations can be pretty vague in Origins, so you'll be forced to use the eagle + tracking, at times, while Odyssey provides a short description of the location, in addition to the eagle.

I did enjoy the exploration and challenges but the new quests were a bit too much time-consuming and the cosmetic rewards weren't really needed so close to the end.

Time for a break before going back to Odyssey and its mysteries of Atlantis.

Assassin's Creed Origins was a really enjoyable experience, especially because I have actually been to Egypt. Seeing places I visited recreated during Ancient Egypt at the height of its civilization was amazing. Walking through Alexandria, Memphis, the pyramids, and the deserts gave me a whole new appreciation for the setting. Ubisoft really did an incredible job bringing Egypt to life.

The main story is good and I really enjoyed Bayek's revenge journey. Bayek is easily one of my favorite Assassin's Creed protagonists, and I also liked Aya whenever she became playable. Their relationship carries the story and gives it a lot of emotional weight. My biggest issue is that the main story feels too short. It feels like only about 30 percent of the game is actually focused on the main plot, while the other 70 percent is side content. I wish there had been more story missions because the revenge plot was one of the strongest parts of the game.

The Hidden Ones DLC was easily my favorite part after the base game. It was great seeing the Brotherhood after the Creed had officially been established. Recruiting new members, expanding the Hidden Ones, and tying up one of the loose ends from the main story made the DLC feel like a proper continuation. It was also nice to see Aya return.

Curse of the Pharaohs was a different experience. The story itself did not really grab me, and once again it felt like most of the content was side quests instead of main missions. However, the mythology and the different afterlife locations were absolutely stunning. Exploring those worlds showed just how creative Ubisoft could be when they were not limited by historical realism.

Combat is where the game disappointed me the most. It is simply too easy. I ended up using a bow build for almost the entire game because headshots would one shot most enemies. Once I filled my adrenaline bar, I could also instantly kill stronger enemies. Melee combat felt much weaker by comparison, so there wa…
Not a fan of rpg games but this was good. My frustrations are with the rpg mechanics and not Origins in general. Stunning visuals, good story albeit pretty short. Combat is also good.

I really wanted to like Assassin's Creed Origins. It is constantly praised as one of the best games in the series, but after finishing it, I was left very disappointed.

For context, I have finished every main Assassin's Creed game except Syndicate, Mirage, and Shadows, and I actually enjoyed both Odyssey and Valhalla more than Origins. My problem isn't that the series became an RPG.

The story never really grabbed me. Half of the game felt like there was no real plot. It finally became interesting once Caesar and Cleopatra became central to it, but it took far too long to get there, and the ending felt underwhelming.

My biggest issue was the gameplay. Stealth felt clunky, assassination animations were slow, there are no double assassinations, and I really disliked that enemies only a few levels above me could survive a hidden blade assassination. If I manage to sneak behind someone and stab them in the neck, they should die. That's the whole point of being an Assassin.

The combat also never clicked with me. It lacked the weight and flow I enjoyed in later RPG entries, heavy weapons felt unsatisfying, and enemy scaling often made fights feel frustrating rather than challenging.

Bayek's voice actor is great, but I never really connected with the character, and after nearly 40 hours I didn't feel like he had changed much.

I know many people love Origins, but I guess I'm not one of them. It ended up being one of the weakest Assassin's Creed games I've played.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe feeling forced to complete side missions and gather crafting materials through hunting to level up and upgrade gear.

citations.review_text:
Parkour in this game is pretty bad, you can climb anything, anywhere. It now lacks depth and it is no longer skill that you learn throught game.
To get enough character level you are forced to complete many side missions, that can be boring, even though they have cutscenes and voice acting. Also to upgrade you need hunting animals and convoys.
Otherwise this is very good game. Enemies will not wait till you kill one of them, instead they will attack if they see chance, so moving is important. Skilltree allows to become archer, warrior and more, even using animals as allies. World is vast and very detailed. Graphics are very good. Story has some interesting plot twists.

I really enjoyed exploring the beautiful world of Ancient Egypt. The graphics still look great, and the cities, deserts, and pyramids create an amazing atmosphere. The story is good, but you are forced to play boring side missions to level up. The combat is enjoyable and fun. I really loved the game.

However, after playing Assassin's Creed Odyssey, Origins feels like a downgrade in some ways. The combat is simpler and has fewer abilities, so battles are less exciting. There is less freedom to customize your character and weapons. The map is also smaller, with fewer activities and less variety compared to Odyssey's huge world and many islands. Traveling and exploring are still enjoyable, but Odyssey offers more content and more ways to play.

Overall, Assassin's Creed Origins is an excellent game with a great story and an unforgettable main character. But if you have already played Odyssey, Origins may feel like a step back because it has fewer gameplay features, less customization, and a smaller world.

My feelings are mixed.

On the positive side of things the setting is amazing and it really is a fresh aesthetic for a different beat on the classic AC trope. It's worth noting that I have played hours of the game... but many aspects annoy me. The constant materials grind to upgrade armour. At the higher levels, it becomes tedious and a chore that I am doing on autopilot. It's not enjoyable play but feels necessary because, the combat feels clunky. Awkward movements or unresponsiveness can sometimes lead to frustrating deaths. 

More annoying still is the loading and account requirements. I had to make a Ubisoft account so that they can spend every waking hour trying to sell me something and of course, most likely, actually sell me in the form of my data. Ubisoft suck for doing this and it diminishes the game. It makes the load time for the game ridiculously long as I assume they try to transmit the contents of my breakfast to their servers. When I tried playing offline, the load times tripled or quadrupled and it still required that I first have a Ubisoft account. Really low level behaviour.

Finally - Microtransactions. I will never microtransact, but their very presence in any game is a major detraction and majorly unethical as many minors may play the game.

So overall, the game has some appeal and I would have recommended it but for Ubisoft injecting marketing poison throughout.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the open world map is oversized and filled with repetitive side quests, activities, and filler content.

citations.review_text:
Assassin's Creed Origins was genuinely enjoyable. I really liked exploring ancient Egypt, as the world felt beautiful and alive. Bayek was a great character, and his journey with Aya was interesting to follow. What I liked most was seeing how their story connects to the origins of the Brotherhood. ⚔️
The combat was fun and satisfying, while exploring tombs, villages, and the desert kept things interesting. Some missions did feel a little repetitive after a while, but it never ruined the experience.
Overall, a great AC game with a beautiful world, memorable characters, and an interesting story worth experiencing. ❤️

Beautiful world, story is fairly interesting. The combat mechanics are decent, and the overall gameplay is enjoyable.

However, the map feels unreasonably huge, and a lot of it is filled with repetitive and uninteresting quests. While there’s plenty to explore, the sheer size of the world can make the experience feel padded at times.

Overall, it’s a solid Assassin’s Creed game with a great setting and an interesting story, but the oversized map and repetitive side content hold it back from being a truly great experience.

Great Game. Main story is short and does not utilize massive parts of the map. Side Quests are fun but rather repetitive in nature. Map is expansive but feels dead-boring at times. Other times the map provides exceptional beauty and stunning realism as objects/\characters near and far interact with the world naturally.

Get the "Enhanced Predator Bow Perk" Early, Unlocks new gameplans, mechanics and possibly the most fun way to take on enemies.

NOT RECOMMENDED!
In short: A beautiful but completely empty shell. Ubisoft created a stunning historical playground but forgot to put an actual game inside. Main Issues: Zero substance.. Beyond the beautiful scenery, the game has absolutely nothing to offer. It is a hollow world filled with tedious, repetitive activities. Terrible story. The plot is a generic, cliché revenge story. The villains are poorly written and shallow—they are just "bad because they are bad" with zero depth. Brain-dead AI. NPCs are incredibly stupid and actively throw themselves under your horse's hooves while you ride. Awful RPG and grind. The level-gating is aggressive. The game forces you into endless, boring grinding just to progress, backed by a shallow and uninteresting RPG system. Poor animations. Character facial animations are stiff, lifeless, and look completely outdated. Lore disrespect. For a game subtitled Origins, the creation of the Brotherhood is handled incredibly superficially. There is no depth to the lore, and the stealth gameplay feels completely ruined with no real room for assassin roleplay. Infinite spawns. You will constantly fight endless hordes of enemies that seemingly spawn out of thin air. 
Verdict: The developers are simply parasitic on the franchise name to sell empty, formulaic products. Do not waste your time and money on this beautiful but soulless grind-fest.

Ancient Egypt is handled beautifully here: The deserts, the cities, the tombs, the pyramids, the Nile, all of it feels alive in a way that can easily pull you in for hours.
The story is actually pretty engaging too (not yet reaching the levels of the Ezio trilogy), and Bayek is a great protagonist, one of the few AC leads that feels genuinely memorable instead of just generic guy with a hidden blade.

The combat is also a big step up from the older games in a lot of ways. You have more weapon variety, more tools and more flexibility in how you approach fights, so even when things get messy it usually feels fun rather than stiff. Exploring tombs and ruins is probably the best part of the game for me, because it hits that perfect mix of mystery, atmosphere.
That said the game is not without its baggage and some of it is hard to ignore, for example the open world is huge but a lot of it is stuffed with filler that starts to feel like busywork after a while. Side quests can be interesting but far too many of them boil down to go here, kill this, fetch that, repeat until your XP bar stops being annoying. The level gating can also kill the pacing because sometimes the main story just pauses and tells you to go grind for a bit, which is never a great feeling in a game that already wants to be taken seriously.

Aaaand of course there is the usual Ubislop nonsense hanging around in the background: microtransactions, forced systems and the creeping feeling that some of the design is there to stretch playtime rather than improve the experience. The Assassin’s Creed identity is also a little watered down here so if you are attached to the old stealth and parkour formula this may feel more like a very good action RPG wearing AC branding than a true classic Assassin’s Creed game. Even the optimization can get a bit shaky, with occasional frame drops reminding you that the sand is not the only thing that is rough around the edges.

Still, despite all that, Origins succeeds because…

I LOVE Egypt, so I was really looking forward to playing this game. And what a disappointment it was...
The game is BORING. I still have not finished the game, even after getting back to is like 3 times already...
The story sucks, some parts of the map are literally empty, basically, 1 hour in, you have seen every activity type in the game. And after that, it is just grinding the "?" marks.
And it is not because of the "new" AC gameplay, I finished The Odyssey with no issues and loved the game..

Assassin’s Creed Origins:

Is a strong entry in the series and a great starting point for the newer RPG-style Assassin’s Creed games.

The Ancient Egypt setting is easily one of the best parts of the game. Exploring deserts, pyramids, tombs, cities, rivers, and hidden locations feels amazing. The world looks great, the music fits the setting well, and Bayek is a strong main character. His story gives the game more emotion, and seeing the beginning of the Assassin Brotherhood makes it important for fans of the series.

The gameplay is fun, but it can be a bit of a grind. Origins changed the series a lot by adding more RPG elements, levels, gear, loot, abilities, and a bigger open world. I enjoyed the combat, exploration, story, and characters, but there are times where you need to do side content to keep up with the level requirements.

Going for 100% completion is fun and fairly easy, but it can still become a grind because there is a lot to clear on the map. If you enjoy open-world games and achievement hunting, it is not too bad, but it does take time.

I would recommend Assassin’s Creed Origins to casual players, achievement hunters, story players, and fans of Assassin’s Creed. It is not perfect, but it is a good game with a great world, strong main character, and fun gameplay.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that parkour mechanics are simplified and stripped down compared to previous titles in the franchise.

citations.review_text:
[h1] Dumbed Down Witcher 3 Clone, with an In-Game Cash Shop! [/h1] 

Gameplay wise, this is no longer Assassin's Creed.  Free-running has been severely dumbed down to where navigating the world is so simplistic it can be mind-numbing at times.  Sure you can still assassinate but that's the last vestige of the 'Assassin' gameplay.

I liked Bayek, I appreciated that he was proven right at one point in the story (and Aya proven wrong), but Aya & Layla are annoying characters.   

The worst thing though is that Ubisoft [b]removed[/b] the ability for the player to buy Heka Crates using the non-paid currency of the game (years ago it seems).   The cash shop isn't purely cosmetics either.   There are cool weapons and armor you can get from normal gameplay, but the fact the Helix Shop is seemingly here to stay in the series is a blight.   Remember, this game has paid DLC as well!  How much are we expected to pay for these games exactly? Hundreds of dollars per title?!?! 

If you were to purchase Helix Credits now, it's not as if the money goes to the artists or programmers involved in the games development via royalties or something.  Nope, just straight to the current execs over at Ubisoft!

Only get this title if you can get it for dirt cheap.

this game has too much content to make an in-depth review so ill just list what i liked and what i didn't

WHAT I LIKED:
the graphics: (most beautiful shi i ever seen)

the map / setting: ANCIENT EGYPT IS AWESOME. i especially really liked the northern part of the map with cyrene, it's just peak

BAYEK: HE'S LITERALLY THE HIGHLIGHT OF THIS GAME. his actor is truly amazing, you can clearly tell every single emotion he's trying to convey.

stealth: not as good as unity, but overall really solid and grounded. the predator bow and the tool variety make up for a smooth stealth experience. i didn't like how the hidden blade can't one shot everything though.

parkour: while it is really stripped down compared to the other ac games, it's still very smooth and flowing, despite not having a lot of moves.

story: it's structured well and has a reasonable pace. the ending is satisfying aswell.

DLC: overall same quality as the story. although i didn't enjoy curse of the pharaohs very much, mostly due to the supernatural stuff. (and those unbalanced bosses with the god awful combat)

photo mode: it makes u feel like a photographer, every single frame in this game is photo-worthy.

WHAT I DIDN'T LIKE:

horse riding: it's really slow and irritating to get from point A to B, and while theres still fast travel, the huge map makes it less effective.

the combat: they tried to mimic soulslike combat, but it just got repetitive after a while, to the point it turns into spamming the instant charged strike to infinitely stun enemies. the bosses were also kinda lame, just damage sponges with no real way to counter their attack patterns.

collectibles: like the combat, they get repetitive after collecting enough and they mostly serve as a distraction from the main quests.

the ENTIRETY of the RPG mechanics: leveling, materials, crafting, all of that adds nothing to the actual game and just makes everything a chore, it would've been better if they made leveling on…
gameplay and combat is cool, but it parkour was too basic and it could have had more assassination animations, but overall its a pretty good game

This game is described by many as the first of the RPG Assassin's Creed games, which are controversial. This also happens to be one of my favorite Assassin's Creed games. 

First of all, it actually has to do with the Assassins, specifically with the start of the Order, so it ties in well to the lore and the rest of the franchise. Second of all, the open world is very immersive and beautiful. It is big but it kept me interested the whole time; I genuinely enjoyed exploring every random location even if just for the sake of it. The story was also pretty good for the most part. I did not really feel like I had to grind to level up and explore higher level locations because I enjoyed doing all the game has to offer, and therefore I was never underleveled.

The only downsides of this game are the combat and parkour. The parkour is not as good as some of the original Assassin's Creed games and there are also not as many places to use it -- the world is wide and you are not always in a dense city. The combat also felt more delayed and unresponsive than it should, this was confirmed when I loaded up AC Odyssey where the combat feels way smoother.

However, these problems are only minor, as I played this game through three separate times and enjoyed each one.
Good game. I miss the old parkour system. Other than that good rpg

claims.claim: Reviewers encounter technical and account issues related to Ubisoft Connect, including account lockouts and controller support failures.

citations.review_text: Controller support is broken so I can't recommend this game. Two different PC's and the same reliability issues. I managed to improve things which I'll elaborate on shortly but why is a nine year old game still broken ? Anyway here's what I did. I took Steam offline and this helped. A game you can't play without an Ubisoft connect account but a game that's unplayable WITH an Ubisoft connect account ??? The mind boggles. As well as doing the above you can also go into the games options and manually select your controller. Mine was previously set to auto switch. After this the issues were 90% fixed. Still a pain in the neck but borderline acceptable. Avoid unless your passion is for acting as Ubisoft technical support.

I loved this game when it came out. I reinstalled last week. Ubisoft locks my account every time I start the game. I either have to reset my password or contact support and wait for them to unlock. Itll work for an evening, then account locked next day. It keeps happening. They never tell me how to prevent it. I just get an email saying it is unlocked. I would suggest not buying any ubisoft products.

Even the optimization can get a bit shaky, with occasional frame drops reminding you that the sand is not the only thing that is rough around the edges.

Still, despite all that, Origins succeeds because…
